topic.title: Rational Functions and Zeros
topic.summary: The real zeros of a rational function, and how the real zeros of its numerator and denominator determine where it is positive or negative.

variants.stem: The rational function r is given by r(x) = (x² − 2x − 15)/(x − 4).

parts.prompt: Find all real zeros of r.
Find the value of x that is not in the domain of r.

solution: A rational function is 0 only where its numerator is 0 and the function is defined. The numerator is 0 at x = −3 and x = 5.
The denominator is 0 at x = 4, so r is undefined there. Neither zero of the numerator equals 4, so both are zeros of r.

variants.stem: The rational function r is given by r(x) = (x² − 3x − 18)/(x − 6).

parts.prompt: Find all real zeros of r.
Write the domain of r in interval notation.

solution: Factor the numerator: x² − 3x − 18 = (x − 6)(x + 3). The numerator is 0 at x = 6 and x = −3.
The denominator is 0 at x = 6, so 6 is not in the domain of r, and it cannot be a zero of r even though it makes the numerator 0.
The only real zero of r is x = −3, and the domain is (−∞, 6) ∪ (6, ∞).

variants.stem: The graph of the rational function r is shown. The graph has a vertical asymptote, drawn as a dashed line, and crosses the x-axis at the two points shown.

stimulusBlocks.caption: The graph of y = r(x)
stimulusBlocks.alt: The graph of a rational function with x-intercepts at x = −4 and x = 4 and a vertical asymptote at x = 2.

parts.prompt: Find all real zeros of r.
Write the set of all x for which r(x) > 0 in interval notation.

solution: The graph crosses the x-axis at x = −4 and x = 4, so those are the real zeros.
The dashed line is at x = 2, where r is undefined. The three values split the number line into intervals.
Reading the graph, r(x) > 0 where the graph is above the x-axis: on (−∞, −4) ∪ (2, 4). The endpoints are not included because r(x) = 0 at the zeros and r is undefined at x = 2.

variants.stem: Solve the inequality (x − 4)/(x − 1) ≤ 0. Write the solution in interval notation.
solution: The numerator is 0 at x = 4, and the denominator is 0 at x = 1.
These values split the number line into 3 intervals. Testing one value in each interval shows that the fraction is positive on (−∞, 1) and (4, ∞), negative on (1, 4).
The inequality allows equality, so include each zero of the numerator that is in the domain. Never include a zero of the denominator, because the fraction is undefined there.
So the solution is (1, 4].

variants.stem: Solve the inequality (x − 5)/(x − 7) ≥ 0. Write the solution in interval notation.

These values split the number line into 3 intervals. Testing one value in each interval shows that the fraction is positive on (−∞, 5) and (7, ∞), negative on (5, 7).
The inequality allows equality, so include each zero of the numerator that is in the domain. Never include a zero of the denominator, because the fraction is undefined there.
So the solution is (−∞, 5] ∪ (7, ∞).

variants.stem: Solve the inequality (x + 2)/(x + 4) < 0. Write the solution in interval notation.

These values split the number line into 3 intervals. Testing one value in each interval shows that the fraction is positive on (−∞, −4) and (−2, ∞), negative on (−4, −2).
The inequality is strict, so no endpoint is included.
So the solution is (−4, −2).

variants.stem: The rational function r is given by r(x) = 3(x − 3)(x − 5)/(x + 1).
